title: The bodhi tree cutting
hookLine: Ashoka's daughter Sanghamitta brings a cutting of the bodhi tree to Anuradhapura, where it still grows

lines: THE WOMEN ASK TO BE ORDAINED.
cards: On the island, a group of women have a request. Anula, a woman of the royal house, and the women around her have heard Mahinda teach, and they want to be ordained as nuns.
Mahinda says he can't: the chronicle has him say it isn't allowed for monks to ordain women. That takes nuns, and there are no nuns on the island. But Mahinda has a sister.
So a message goes back across the sea to the emperor, asking for two things: his daughter, and a branch of a tree.

teach.b: First, the sister. Sanghamitta is a nun, Ashoka's daughter, and in the Mahavamsa she agrees to go. She can give the island's women what they asked for.
Second, the branch. It comes from the bodhi tree, under which the Buddha sat the night he awoke.

teach.h: A BRANCH IN A GOLDEN VESSEL.
teach.b: The chronicle tells of a branch taken with great ceremony and set in a golden vessel, carried to the coast and onto a ship, with Sanghamitta beside it: music, offerings, the sea itself, it says, made calm.

teach.h: THE KING WADES INTO THE SEA.
teach.b: When the ship comes in, King Devanampiya Tissa wades into the water up to his neck to receive the branch. There's the image: a king, soaked, holding a pot with a tree in it over his head.
The branch is carried to the royal capital, Anuradhapura, and planted in a park there. And Anula and the women around her are ordained by Sanghamitta. The tree and the nuns arrive together.

Fourth, it still grows. At Anuradhapura today, a bodhi tree stands behind railings, held up by props, surrounded by flags and pilgrims. Tradition holds that it is that same tree, grown from the branch Sanghamitta brought.

Pilgrims sit near it, offer flowers, and pour water at its roots. Historians may ask what can be proven. The people beneath it honor something simpler: a living thing cared for by many hands, for a very long time.

how: Pilgrims visit the bodhi tree at Anuradhapura to offer flowers and water and to sit in meditation, and Sri Lankan Buddhists remember Sanghamitta's arrival at a full moon festival each year.

the golden vessel that carried the sacred branch
Ashoka's daughter, a nun who brought the bodhi branch

s: Sanghamitta came so the island's women could be ordained
Mahinda said monks couldn't ordain them; that took a nun, and she was one.
the bodhi tree came to the island as a seed

games.q: you're the island's king. the ship carrying the branch of the bodhi tree is coming in to shore. what do you do?
o: wait on the shore for it to be brought to you.
wade into the sea to receive it.
send a minister to fetch it.
games.why: the chronicle says the king waded in up to his neck to receive the branch.

practice: Go to a plant if one is near, or bring one to mind, a houseplant, a tree on your street, weeds pushing through a sidewalk, and give it a little water if it needs it, or just look closely: the color of the leaves, where it grows toward the light.
Then let it keep you company while you sit, something alive and slowly growing while you stay still.

wordCard.voice: Sanghamitta. Ashoka's daughter, a nun who carried a branch of the bodhi tree across the sea to Anuradhapura.

orig.note: Pali and Sanskrit: bodhi, awakening; the tree is named for what happened beneath it.

carryVoice: Your line: it still grows. Many hands have tended it since. Day eight hundred sixty-two.

sources.ref: Mahavamsa 15, 18–19 (Anula's request; the bodhi branch and Sanghamitta)
